items.heading: Three Paths Get Lumped Together
items.text: Three paths get lumped together in most advice on this topic, and they are not the same decision. Joining a consulting firm means selling your time inside someone else's brand, method, and client roster, with structured training and a career ladder built for people who are still developing deep expertise. Generalist freelancing means executing a defined task for a client who directs the work, priced mostly against how many other people could do it too.

items.heading: Before Pricing, Branding, or Client
items.text: Before pricing, branding, or client outreach matter at all, run The 3-Pillar Readiness Check: expertise depth, existing network reach, and financial runway. Weak on any one of these and the whole plan gets shaky fast, no matter how good your actual work is.

items.heading: The Economics of Independent Consulting
items.text: The economics of independent consulting are structurally different from freelancing, and understanding that difference changes how you should price and sell your work from day one.
